Remarks (added by pf02, June 2026)[edit]

: The solution given above is incorrect.

The main error is in the statement "since ... each positive integer is expressible as , ... we obtain that ". The conclusion does not follow from the hypothesis, and in fact, the conclusion is false. As pointed out on the discussion page by anh1110004, take for example . One can easily see that , but . An even simpler counterexample is , but (The details for these numbers will be given below, in Solution 3.).

Besides this, part of the proof that is incorrect. (If we want to be generous and give the benefit of the doubt, we could say that the proof is incomprehensible. I for one, could make no sense of it, but I am convinced that it is incorrect.)

To top these errors, there are a lot of hand waving, unproven and unjustified statements, and many minor errors in the statements. And the editing is so poor that it brings to shame mathematical writing.

However, the author (pohoatza) is to be lauded for pointing out that the Fibonacci numbers play a special role in this problem.
